text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A commission of inquiry into legislation on combating crime has proposed rastic amendments putting greater emphasis on the rights of victims of crime. Judge Bryan O'Linn said victims' interests should be considered from the complaint phase, during bail proceedings and until the end of trial. The commission of inquiry was set up in response to increased in crime in Namibia.

- The main Namibian opposition party DTA has vowed to do what it can to stop the controversial Epupa hydro-electric power project, saying it was clear that residents in the north-western Kunene region were opposed to it.

- Stricter control and discipline were being implemented at Windhoek central prison after three trial-awaiting prisoners boycotted court proceedings. The committee representing awaiting trial detainees said last week that inmates would embark on a hunger strike if demands for a meeting with the ministries of home affairs and justice were not met.
- The finance ministers of Namibia and South Africa have signed a bilateral agreement cancelling Namibia's pre- independence debt to its neighbour.
